**All clear** — no blocking ambiguities. Proceeding to `planning`.

The body's one open fork ("decide first, wire second") is a design-preference
call, which under `EPM_AUTONOMOUS_SESSION=1` is this session's to make, not a
block reason (`.claude/rules/auto-continuation.md` § STATE-TO-`blocked`
criterion 1, autonomous carve-out). Decision stated below; the plan +
critic round is the check on it.

## Context resolved

- **Wire target located.** `scripts/autonomous_session_watch.py` (35,234 lines):
  the pure decision fn is `decide_pod_safety` (:4093), its caller `_process_pod`
  (:18672) computes the two existing exemptions via `_escaped_pod_exemptions`
  (:18643), and `_apply_pod_safety_action` (:18848) dispatches the five actions.
  `POD_SAFETY_AUTO_STOP` (:1454) = `AUTO_STOP_DONE | AUTO_STOP_PAUSED`. The
  strongest action on this arm is a reversible `pod.py stop` — never a
  terminate.
- **#2277's readers are directly importable.** The watcher ALREADY imports from
  `pod_lifecycle` (`from pod_lifecycle import _is_managed_pod,
  _issue_from_pod_name`, :1228), so the four fence readers —
  `_pod_evidence_window` (:3787), `_latest_pod_token` (:3803),
  `_latest_pod_fence_until` (:3827), `_latest_pass_owner_for_pod` (:3876) —
  are reusable with no new parse. The banned-direction import
  (`pod_lifecycle` → watcher) is the one #2277 avoided with its one-line
  `_pod_named_pattern` copy; this direction is already established.
- **No pure predicate exists yet.** `_guard_owner_fence_before_terminate`
  (:3903) inlines the fence-active-and-unwaived test and `raise SystemExit`s,
  so it cannot be called from a watcher pass. Plan will extract the predicate
  and have the guard call it — one source of truth, no second parser (the
  defect class #2277's own review round flagged).
- **The existing shields already cover part of the gap.** `followup_active`
  (`_task_followup_active`) skips the stop when an `epm:run-launched` is newer
  than the latest done-transition — and a fence is registered on
  `epm:run-launched` / `epm:progress` notes. So a fence riding a fresh
  `run-launched` is ALREADY shielded today. The residual gap is narrower than
  the body's framing: a fence on an `epm:progress` note only, or a fence whose
  `run-launched` predates a later done-transition (the watcher's re-arm
  semantics flipping the inferred shield off).
- **No observed harm from this path.** On 2026-08-13 the pass logged three
  `pod-keep-running-skip` exemptions against the incident pods — it did not
  stop them. The harm was inflicted by a non-owner `pod.py terminate`, which
  #2277 closed. This task closes a latent gap, not a live bleeding one.
- **House precedent for bounding a self-service shield.** The #1961 per-pod
  named shield is ceiling-bounded (`EPM_POD_NAMED_SHIELD_MAX_AGE_H`, 48h); the
  #1582 keep-running wedged-owner arm escalates a tagged pod with a provably
  wedged owner. Both are the pattern for "honour the signal, bound the
  window".

## Decision: bounded DEFER + ESCALATE, not unbounded suppress

Wire it, but as a **time-bounded deferral with escalation**, not a
`keep-running`-style unconditional skip.

- **Why not plain suppress.** Unlike the `keep-running` tag, a fence is a token
  any session can self-post with no operator action. An unconditional
  fence-skip creates an unbounded self-service pod-alive shape with no
  wedged-owner arm behind it — the fence-refresh-forever risk row in #2277
  plan §8, on the one pass whose entire purpose is reclaiming spend from
  provably parked/terminal tasks.
- **Why not surface-only.** Surfacing without deferring leaves the stop to
  land, so it does not close the stated Goal harm (an in-flight owner round
  interrupted) at all.
- **Shape.** When the status-class arm would `stop` a pod that carries an
  UNEXPIRED fence AND whose latest pod-bound PASS lacks the matching `owner=`
  (the terminate guard's exact predicate — owner presumed live), DEFER the
  stop and escalate once per episode (marker + push + sidecar) naming the pod,
  the fence expiry, and the hourly burn. Two bounds: the fence's own
  `fence_until` (primary — expiry re-arms the ordinary auto-stop by
  construction) and a cumulative per-(issue, pod_id) deferral ceiling that
  closes refresh-forever, with a loud escalation at the ceiling.
- **Directionally safe.** The arm can only ever DEFER a stop, never accelerate
  one, so no watcher path becomes more willing to stop a pod than it is today
  (the standing pod directive). Fail-open on every unreadable input (#2277's
  posture); kill switch for rollback; the ≥2-miss accumulation,
  `keep-running` shield, follow-up-signal predicate, and #1961 per-pod named
  shield all preserved unchanged.

Non-goals unchanged: `pod.py terminate` is not re-opened, and the declared
copied-token residual (unauthenticated string equality) stays open under the
same accidents-not-adversaries trust model.
